(Columbia, South Carolina) | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = 2022–2023 | team1 = [[Overtime Elite|YNG Dreamerz]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team2 = [[Wisconsin Herd]] | years3 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = [[Rip City Remix]] | years4 = {{nbay|2024|full=y}} | team4 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years5 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team5 = →[[Texas Legends]] | years6 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team6 = Texas Legends | years7 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team7 = [[Oklahoma City Blue]] | highlights = }} '''Jazian Gortman''' (\JAY-zee-in GORT-min\; born March 14, 2003){{cite web|title=Jazian Gortman G-League Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gortmja01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 23, 2024}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player, currently a free agent. Gortman last played for the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] in the [[NBA G League]]. ==High school career== Gortman attended [[Richland County School District One|W. J. Keenan]] in [[Columbia, South Carolina]] where he averaged 23.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 3.3 steals per outing, being considered a 5-star prospect.{{cite web|first=Jonas|last=Panerio|title=Milwaukee Bucks sign point guard Jazian Gortman|url=https://www.si.com/nba/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-point-guard-jazian-gortman|website=SI.com|date=July 19, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Reggie|last=Anderson|title=Jazian Gortman leaving W.J. Keenan High, turning pro|url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/high-school/jazian-gortman-wj-keenan-high-turning-professional/101-b7474da1-7f01-4617-9242-61eec11e0763|website=WLTX.com|date=August 11, 2021|access-date=July 23, 2024}} However, before his senior season, he decided to leave high school and turn pro. ==Professional career== ===YNG Dreamerz (2022–2023)=== On August 11, 2021, Gortman signed with the [[Overtime Elite|YNG Dreamerz]] of the [[Overtime Elite]] ahead of the 2022–2023 season. In his first season as a pro, he averaged 13.9 points, 3.9 assists, 4.8 rebounds, and 2.5 steals per game. ===Wisconsin Herd (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Gortman joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks announce roster for NBA 2K24 Summer League 2023|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-announce-roster-for-nba-2k24-summer-league-2023|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2024}} and on July 15, he signed with them.{{cite tweet|author=Bucks Muse|title=The 2023 Milwaukee Bucks official 21 man training camp roster|number=1708846920045559876|user=BucksMuse|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2024}} However, he was waived on October 18{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks request waivers on three players|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-request-waivers-on-three-players|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2024}} and twelve days later, he joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCE 2023 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2024}} In 18 games, he averaged 6.9 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 14.7 minutes.{{cite web|title=Jazian Gortman Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jazian-Gortman/Summary/176050|website=RealGM.com|access-date=July 23, 2024}} ===Rip City Remix (2024)=== On January 12, 2024, Gortman was traded to the [[Rip City Remix]] for [[Malachi Smith (basketball)|Malachi Smith]],{{cite tweet|author=Rip City Remix|title=Rip City Remix have acquired Jazian Gortman in exchange for Malachi Smith.💿|number=1745960282495848522|user=ripcityremix|date=January 12, 2024|access-date=July 23, 2024}} playing in 23 games and averaging 10.5 points, 2.7 rebounds and 4.2 assists in 21.2 minutes. ===Dallas Mavericks / Texas Legends (2024–2025)=== On July 12, 2024, Gortman signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], joined them for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]{{cite tweet|first=Mike|last=Curtis|title=Mavs announce they’ve signed guard Jazian Gortman and forward Emanuel Miller. Both players will play for the team’s Summer League squad. Mavs SL coach Jared Dudley said today that Miller is one of the most physical players on the team.|number=1811913501071540495|user=MikeACurtis2|date=July 12, 2024|access-date=July 23, 2024}} and on October 18, his deal was converted into a [[two-way contract]]. After his contract conversion. Gortman appeared in 16 games for the Mavericks averaging 1.5 points.{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today that they have converted Jazian Gortman to a Two-Way contract.|number=1847427891253944591|user=MavsPR|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Dwain|last=Price|title=Jazian Gortman’s journey has paid off with two-way contract|url=https://www.mavs.com/gortmanearnedtwo-waycontract/|website=Mavs.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On January 26, 2025, Gortman was waived by the Mavericks{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today that they have signed center Kylor Kelley to a Two-Way contract and requested waivers on Two-Way guard Jazian Gortman. Kelley will wear No. 50 for the Mavericks.|number=1883658844515316024|user=MavsPR|date=January 26, 2025|access-date=January 26, 2025}} and three days later, joined the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|first=Mylles|last=Royals|title=MAVERICKS SIGN KYLOR KELLEY TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/mavericks-sign-kylor-kelley-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2025|access-date=January 31, 2025}} ===Oklahoma City / Oklahoma City Blue (2025)=== On Friday, September 26, 2025, the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] acquired the rights to Gortman in exchange for a 2026 first-round pick and a 2026 second-round pick.{{cite tweet | user=CAlmanza1007 | number=1971623130272878793 | author=C. Almanza | date= | title=The Oklahoma City Blue has acquired the returning player rights to guard Jazian Gortman from the Texas Legends in exchange for a 2026 first-round pick and a 2026 second-round pick, the team announced today. | url=https://x.com/CAlmanza1007/status/1971623130272878793 | access-date=October 7, 2025 | work=Twitter | language=en}}{{cite web | last=RotoWire Staff | title=Thunder's Jazian Gortman: Signed by Oklahoma City | website=CBSSports | date=September 26, 2025 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-jazian-gortman-signed-by-oklahoma-city/ | access-date=October 7, 2025}}{{cite web | last=Simone | first=Jack | title=Thunder just signed another steal if track record proves true | website=Thunderous Intentions | date=2025 | url=https://thunderousintentions.com/oklahoma-city-thunder-sign-chris-youngblood-contract-next-steal-track-record-three-pointers-summer-league-training-camp-zack-austin-jazian-gortman | access-date=October 7, 2025}} On October 6, Gortman made his [[pre-season]] debut against his former team, the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]], where he scored 12 points, along with four rebounds, and two assists.{{cite web | last=Burton | first=Cody | title=Mavericks Edge By Thunder Despite Late Comeback Attempt | website=Sports Illustrated | date=October 6, 2025 |
